text: 🍿 Supergirl hits HBO Max September 10. The discourse is already warming up. 📆 Estreno: September 10, 2026 (HBO Max) 🎭 Género: #Superhero · #SciFi · #DCU ✈️ Add to watchlist Milly Alcock is genuinely good casting. A jaded, punk-edged Kara with real bite, nothing like the blue-eyed scout of old. What drags the film down is everything around her: the script, the palette, that oppressive murky brown and yellow grade that makes every frame look like it was shot inside a diesel engine. Director Craig Gillespie reportedly skipped Tom King and Bilquis Evely's source comic entirely before taking the job. It shows. The book's visual poetry is striking; the film's is not. Deliberately ignoring your source material isn't a bold creative choice, it's just hubris with receipts.

🍿 The Angry Birds Movie 3 rips off the Dune poster and somehow earns it 📆 Estreno: December 23, 2026 🎭 Género: #Animation · #Comedy · #Family ✈️ Add to watchlist "Lisan al Birdee." That poster is funnier than most blockbuster marketing this year. Director John Rice and Jason Sudeikis are leaning hard into self-awareness, and it works. The first The Angry Birds Movie had no business being as funny as it was. Solid jokes, real craft underneath the IP slop. Three films in, the franchise is still betting on meme culture as its engine, and honestly, that bet looks smarter every time.

🧠 Idiocracy turns 20. It was right about everything except the timeline. Mike Judge gave President Camacho 500 years to emerge. We're speedrunning it in real time. The film's sharpest joke isn't the Brawndo ads or the toilet humor, it's that Camacho actually listened to an expert when it counted. That's the detail that stings most in 2026. Idiocracy didn't predict collapse or dictatorship. It predicted a world that stays just functional enough to keep humiliating itself, and somehow that's the scarier outcome. ✈️ Add to watchlist
